children: University of Pennsylvania law professor Amy Wax has added prominent conservative attorney John Eastman to the team of lawyers representing her in her high-profile discrimination lawsuit against the university.

Eastman filed a court notice that he's joining the case for Wax last week, five months after California stripped him of his law license in the state over his efforts to overturn U.S. President Donald Trump's 2020 election loss to Democrat Joe Biden.

The Philadelphia-based 3rd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, where Wax’s case is pending, maintains its own bar of approved attorneys. A court database shows Eastman has been a member of the Third Circuit bar since 2017.

In a statement to Reuters on Monday, Eastman said his California disbarment was "so obviously political" that he does not expect any issues with the 3rd Circuit, adding that he is "delighted" to represent Wax.
"In many ways, Penn’s efforts to cancel [Wax] are part of a broader, despicable cancel culture of which my own Cal Bar proceedings are a part," he said.
A Penn spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment, nor did the university’s lead attorney, Michael Kenneally of Morgan, Lewis & Bockius.
Eastman will argue Wax's appeal at a 3rd Circuit hearing in November, according to a filing in the case on Friday.

Wax, who is white, sued the university in January 2025, alleging Penn violated her tenure rights in October 2024 when it suspended her from teaching for one year following an investigation into public statements she made about minority groups.
She claimed that the university is quicker to discipline white people under its free speech policy while overlooking similar conduct by racial minorities. She has also denied allegations of racism.

A federal judge in Philadelphia dismissed the case in August 2025, calling her racial bias claims “implausible.” Wax appealed to the 3rd Circuit in January 2026, claiming the judge improperly relied on Penn’s characterization of “hotly disputed facts” in disciplinary reports about her controversial statements concerning race and that the judge defined retaliation too narrowly. Penn has asked the court to dismiss the case.

A social welfare law and policy scholar, Wax has taught at Penn’s prestigious law school since 2001, and has clashed for years with administrators. Students and faculty first called for her firing in 2017, after she co-authored a newspaper opinion piece arguing that Anglo-Protestant cultural norms are superior.

Eastman is a former law professor and dean at Chapman University in California who represented Trump in a long-shot lawsuit at the U.S. Supreme Court that sought to invalidate votes in four states where the Republican former president had falsely claimed widespread 2020 voter fraud.

Eastman also drafted legal memos weeks after the election suggesting then-Vice President Mike Pence could refuse to accept electoral votes from several swing states when Congress convened to certify the vote count. ‌Pence rebuffed his arguments, saying he did not have legal authority to do so under the U.S. Constitution.

The California Supreme Court disbarred Eastman in April after the state bar court that oversees lawyers concluded that he violated California attorney ethics rules against misleading courts and making false public statements.
